s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal distension with early satiety and urinary urgency
salient_findings: Large midline intraperitoneal cyst compressing adjacent abdominal organs
key_facts: 23-year-old woman
2-year history of progressive abdominal distension
Early satiety
Urinary urgency
No pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms
Normal menstrual cycles
Mother had a history of ovarian cysts
Abdomen distended with dull percussion notes
No tenderness or guarding on examination
Large cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm on ultrasonography
Cyst extended from liver to pelvis and involved uterus and ovaries on CT
Fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units
No calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations on CT
Normal laboratory studies, including tumor markers

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large cyst with benign features and family history of ovarian cysts

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst's size and location are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign nature of the cyst and normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: Peritoneal inclusion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst's location and involvement of adjacent organs

shortlist.label: Mesenteric cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst's size and location in the abdominal cavity

shortlist.label: Omental cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst's benign features and possible origin from omental tissue

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Cyst's fluid density and lack of solid components

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the cyst's size and location

raw.rationale: The large size of the cyst, its fluid density, and the absence of calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations on CT are consistent with a mucinous cystadenoma, a type of benign ovarian neoplasm that can grow to be quite large and cause symptoms due to compression of adjacent organs.

rejected.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses both serous and mucinous types, and the specific characteristics of the cyst are more suggestive of a mucinous cystadenoma.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more complex appearance on imaging, including septations and solid components, which are not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Peritoneal inclusion cyst
rejected.why: Usually associated with a history of abdominal surgery or trauma, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Mesenteric cyst
rejected.why: Would not typically involve the uterus and ovaries, and its location is usually more localized to the mesentery.

rejected.label: Omental cyst
rejected.why: Would not typically extend from the liver to the pelvis or involve the uterus and ovaries.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a multilocular appearance on imaging and is less likely to cause symptoms due to compression of adjacent organs.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more complex appearance on imaging, including calcifications, fat, and soft-tissue components, which are not seen in this case.
